settings.title: Flat-Fee Nil T2 Filing for Inactive Trucking Corporations

settings.editor:
Keeping an owner-operator corporation filed while you are off the road can feel like money for nothing, especially with a business number still open, often a fuel tax account beside it, and a truck that may or may not still be in the yard. We file nil T2 returns for exactly those years at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, so the entity stays clean for whenever you go back.

Whether you are off with a back injury, held up by a licence issue, driving for a carrier on payroll, or waiting out a market that turned, we test the year against loads hauled, equipment sold and plate, insurance or storage costs, then prepare and transmit the return. Any year with a disposal in it is sent to the right service instead.

Most owner-operators mean to go back to it, and the corporation is kept for exactly that reason. A filing gap is the thing that makes going back awkward later.

Each year off the road is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. Filing them in order keeps the capital cost allowance on the truck carrying forward, which is what matters on the day it is finally sold.

settings.title: Which T2 Schedules an Inactive Trucking Corporation Files

settings.editor:
ScheduleWhat it reportsOn a nil yearWhy
Schedule 100Balance sheet informationRequiredA truck on the books is an asset, and any loan against it is a liability. There is always a balance sheet to report.
Schedule 125Income statement informationRequiredReports nil revenue and nil expenses for a year with no hauling and nothing claimed.
Schedule 141Notes checklistRequiredAccompanies Schedules 100 and 125 and records who prepared the financial information.
Schedule 50Shareholder informationRequiredOwner-operator corporations are usually held by one person, sometimes with a spouse. Anyone at 10% or more is listed.
Schedule 24First-time filer informationFirst return onlyFiled with the first T2 after incorporation and not again.
Schedule 8Capital cost allowanceRequired while the truck is ownedThis is the schedule that matters here. It carries the undepreciated balance forward year to year, which is what the eventual sale is measured against.

Source: the schedule requirements the Canada Revenue Agency sets for a T2 return, applied to an owner-operator corporation holding depreciable property and hauling nothing. Last reviewed November 19, 2026.

settings.html:
The year is nil

  • No load was hauled and no settlement was received in the tax year
  • The truck and any trailer stayed on the books, unsold
  • No plates, insurance, storage or repair cost was claimed
  • No capital cost allowance was claimed for the year
  • No driver or owner was paid out of the corporation

The year is not nil

  • The tractor, a trailer or any equipment was sold or traded
  • Any carrier settlement arrived, even for a part year
  • Insurance, storage or plate costs were charged to the corporation
  • A fuel tax refund or insurance rebate was received
  • The corporation paid a wage, a dividend or a draw

Due either way

  • The T2 return, for every year until dissolution
  • A T183CORP signed by an authorised signing officer, per tax year
  • Schedule 8, carrying the undepreciated balance on the truck forward
  • Any open fuel tax or GST/HST account, on its own schedule
  • The provincial or federal annual return, a separate registry filing

settings.title: Trucking Corporation Filing Across Canada

settings.editor:
Inactive trucking corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.
